decision: A bucket whose replies keep being length-stopped now earns the same three-strike bench as one whose replies keep failing to parse; input-size refusals are left alone.
how: FOR: the unparseable branch's own comment names 'an output cap it keeps hitting' as the reliably-unusable bucket the bench exists for, yet the length-stopped refusal returned with no strike, so such a bucket was re-claimed on every call for ever. It now shares _UNPARSEABLE (consecutive count, reset by any parseable reply) and the 60 s exponential _bury. AGAINST: the cut may be one caller's max_tokens rather than the bucket's, so benching could shelter a bucket that is fine for other callers; the consecutive reset and the 60 s first bench bound that cost to one minute. The size-refusal half (Groq TPM Requested > Limit) is kept: those already teach the router a ceiling through learn_output_ceiling / box size_refused, which is the correct response to an input-size fact, and a bench would punish the bucket for the caller's prompt size.

decision: On success, _clear() now runs on the bucket that actually answered; the pinned bucket is cleared only when the served bucket cannot be resolved.
how: FOR: _clear's docstring is 'a bucket that just answered is not down', and clearing the pinned bucket when a neighbour served the call erased the evidence that the pinned one did not answer, so a bucket alternating deadline misses with failover successes never climbed past the first 60 s bench. AGAINST: strikes are only earned on the deadline return path, not on a failover, so nothing was strictly owed to the pinned bucket for that call, and clearing the pinned bucket is harmless when it 429ed for a transient reason. The wrong bucket paying is the deciding point; the fallback keeps the old behaviour when _bucket_of returns empty, so no caller sees a change unless a failover actually happened.

decision: dead_forever() keeps returning an empty set once the proof is over PROOF_TTL old.
how: AGAINST (keeping the exclusion past the TTL, the tightening): a stalled prover would then leave every proven-dead bucket excluded, so the pool stays narrow on the resource this file calls the binding constraint. FOR keeping: the TTL is a documented, deliberate rule ('a proof older than an hour is not evidence about now'), and an owner rotating a dead key must be able to see the bucket come back without anyone re-running the prover, which is why the process memo was made freshness-aware. The fail-open is bounded: a genuinely still-dead key is caught again on its next live call by permanent_refusal, which benches it for AUTH_BENCH, and the four owner-hand-excluded buckets in OWNER_EXCLUDED do not lapse. The cost of a lapse is one wasted claim per dead bucket per bench period, not a wrong answer.

decision: repass_bands stays on pipeline.records(); a purged, entry-less record is not re-gated here.
how: FOR changing: a purged record keeps its source-level synthesis, so a band there is never re-checked. AGAINST, and decisive: I measured the live data. Six records have empty entries; exactly one (lost-mines-of-phandelver, status 'purged: wrong fiction') carries a band (M4), and its evidence passes valid_scale_note, so re-gating it would demote nothing. The real defect is that hostcheck.purge leaves a wrong-fiction synthesis behind, which is that module's to fix, not this re-pass. Including empties would also mean a second record reader plus write_record on entry-less records (its drift guard is built around entry counts), for zero live cases. Observation for the coordinator: the leftover M4 on that purged record is wrong-fiction text and belongs to the purge path.

decision: Added an escalation.assert_clear halt interlock to address_space.main (on the SHELFMARKS.json write path) and pantheon.main (before its write).
how: FOR leaving them: both outputs are derived and regenerable, so a halt-time write is recoverable. FOR adding: a halt means a library-wide invariant is broken, both files are read as current by pipeline.py / standards.py or by whoever opens them, and the 2026-09-28 ruling already puts every hand-run writer under the halt; the price is one re-run after the halt lifts. It tightens, so it is in scope. Each is a local _assert_not_halted using the house pattern (fail closed on the escalation import). address_space asks after the placeholder refusal and before the moved-address comparison and the write, so the printed preview still works under a halt; pantheon always writes, so it asks right after argument parsing.

decision: A source declared by more than one record file is no longer repaired from either: its roll row is left as it was and counted as unchecked.
how: Options were: (a) keep last-alphabetical-wins, (b) prefer the file with more entries, (c) refuse to guess. (a) lets a stub that sorts last set the count to 0, which reads 'uncatalogued' and queues re-cataloguing a healthy source. (b) can crown a stale fuller copy over a deliberately purged one. (c) costs only that one row not being refreshed until a person reconciles the files, which the run already names. Chose (c) as the fail-closed option; the dupes report now says so. No live duplicates exist today, so nothing changes on current data.
